jurisdiction.name: Rwanda
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Rwanda governs AI through its National AI Policy, approved by the Cabinet in 2023 and led by the Ministry of ICT and Innovation (MINICT), which also published an AI readiness and maturity framework and, with Singapore, an AI Playbook for Small States. Binding rules come from the 2021 data protection law, which gives people rights over decisions based solely on automated processing. A National AI Agency, central-bank AI risk guidelines and a revision of the ICT law to cover AI are in progress but not yet officially published.
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from documents read in full on official sites. The central bank's 2026 AI risk management guidelines, the National AI Agency and the ICT law revision are listed as leads to check later.

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of ICT and Innovation (MINICT), developed with the Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority (RURA)
instruments.current_status: Listed on MINICT's Policies page, which presents 'policies approved by the Cabinet'; the file is dated 27 April 2023 there and the document's back cover reads 'MINICT - 2022'. The Cabinet communiqué approving it (reported as 20 April 2023) is not on the Prime Minister's Office cabinet-decisions archive, so only the month is recorded. It remains the current national AI policy; in 2026 the Cabinet was reported to have approved a National AI Agency to take it forward (see leads).
instruments.summary: Rwanda's national AI policy, developed by MINICT and RURA, with the vision of becoming a global centre for AI research and innovation and Africa's 'AI Lab and Responsible AI Champion'. It sets six priority areas (skills and AI literacy, infrastructure and compute, a data strategy, trustworthy AI adoption in the public sector, private-sector adoption, and practical AI ethical guidelines) with 14 key recommendations and an implementation plan assigning actions to MINICT, RURA, RISA, NCSA and others. It proposes a Responsible AI Office within MINICT to lead implementation, revised ICT procurement guidelines for AI, and annually updated AI ethical guidelines.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Rwanda's core AI governance instrument; anchors public-sector AI adoption, ethics guidelines and the proposed Responsible AI Office.
metadata_gaps: Exact Cabinet approval date (official communiqué not located)

instruments.official_title: AI Readiness and Maturity Framework for Rwanda
instruments.english_title: AI Readiness and Maturity Framework for Rwanda
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of ICT and Innovation (MINICT), with the Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution Rwanda (C4IR) and GIZ FAIR Forward
instruments.current_status: Listed on MINICT's Policies page with the file dated 21 November 2023; the document itself carries no publication date, so only the month of the official listing is recorded.
instruments.summary: A data-driven framework and dashboard developed by MINICT with C4IR and GIZ FAIR Forward to monitor Rwanda's readiness and maturity in implementing the National AI Policy. It maps indicators drawn from international AI indices (Oxford, Stanford, Tortoise) plus Rwanda-specific indicators onto the policy's six priority areas and reports a first-round assessment. It recommends building data-governance mechanisms and capacity around the dashboard and a scaling strategy for regular reassessment.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Government-published AI readiness assessment tied to monitoring the National AI Policy.
metadata_gaps: Exact publication date (only the official listing month)

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of ICT and Innovation (MINICT) of Rwanda and the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) of Singapore, under the Digital Forum of Small States (Digital FOSS)
instruments.current_status: Published 22 September 2024 (date stated on the cover); listed on MINICT's Policies page. A jointly authored international compilation, not a Rwandan policy with domestic effect.
instruments.summary: A playbook co-developed by Rwanda's MINICT and Singapore's IMDA for the Digital Forum of Small States, compiling how small states have implemented AI strategies and policies. It is organised in four chapters: laying key building blocks, driving AI development and use, fostering a trusted environment, and forging global partnerships, with country case studies including Rwanda's National AI Policy and skills efforts. It offers non-binding practices for policymakers rather than obligations.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Rwanda's international AI-governance cooperation output, published by MINICT.

instruments.official_title: Law Nº 058/2021 of 13/10/2021 relating to the protection of personal data and privacy
instruments.english_title: Law No. 058/2021 of 13 October 2021 relating to the protection of personal data and privacy
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of the Republic of Rwanda (promulgated by the President of the Republic)
instruments.current_status: Published in Official Gazette nº Special of 15/10/2021 in Kinyarwanda, English and French; Article 70 provides that it comes into force on publication. The Gazette copy is hosted on MINICT's Laws page.
instruments.summary: Rwanda's general data protection law, setting principles, lawful bases, data-subject rights, controller and processor obligations, cross-border transfer rules and sanctions, supervised by the public authority in charge of cyber security. Article 21 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects, with exceptions for explicit consent, contracts and authorisation by law with safeguards, and bars such evaluation from relying on sensitive data unless an Article 10 ground applies. It applies to processing in Rwanda and to processing of data of persons in Rwanda by those outside it.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rules on automated decision-making and profiling that govern AI systems processing personal data.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full 82-page Official Gazette PDF read (pdftotext); Article 21 and Article 70 checked

organizations.name: Ministry of ICT and Innovation
organizations.ai_governance_role: Ministry of Information Communication Technology and Innovation (MINICT); lead ministry for AI policy. Developed the National AI Policy with RURA, publishes the AI Readiness and Maturity Framework, and co-authored the Digital FOSS AI Playbook for Small States with Singapore's IMDA. The National AI Policy proposes a Responsible AI Office within MINICT to lead implementation.

organizations.name: Parliament of the Republic of Rwanda
organizations.ai_governance_role: Legislature; adopted Law Nº 058/2021 relating to the protection of personal data and privacy, which includes a right not to be subject to solely automated decisions (Article 21).

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Rwanda's laws, the ICT ministry, the Prime Minister's office, ministries and regulators were searched. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for risk and assurance, procurement, cybersecurity, transparency, standards, sandboxes, sectoral rules, generative AI, drafts, international agreements or historical publications. The central bank's 2026 AI risk management guidelines are a lead, and the Cabinet approvals of the National AI Agency and the National AI Policy are still to be confirmed.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Method note (original): This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from documents read in full on official sites. The central bank's document listings and the cybersecurity authority's website could not be accessed, so the bank's 2026 AI risk management guidelines could not be read. These guidelines, the National AI Agency and the ICT law revision are tracked as leads.

Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. bnr.rw listings JS-rendered, API host HTTP 521; ncsa.gov.rw TLS name mismatch (dpo.gov.rw used). AI policy dated 2023-04 (MINICT file 27 Apr 2023; cover 'MINICT - 2022'; Cabinet approval 20 Apr 2023 secondary only). Readiness Framework dated by listing 2023-11. Playbook (MINICT + IMDA) recategorised from international to government-governance/public-sector at merge. BNR Reg 41/2022 sandbox: text has no AI/emerging-technology provision (AI/ML only a form tick-box) - moved to leads at merge. Renamed i-085796b953cc and o-e56b3f3d9c08. Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: MINICT Laws page (Gazette copies: data protection law, ICT law, cybercrime law, digital ID law); Official Gazette/parliament searched via web search for AI laws and bills: only the data protection law (Art. 21 automated decisions) has AI-relevant provisions; no AI law or AI bill found (ICT law revision announced, held as lead).; Government: MINICT AI page and Policies listing (National AI Policy, AI Readiness and Maturity Framework, AI Playbook for Small States; National Data Sharing Policy 2025 only mentions AI in passing, not recorded); Prime Minister's Office cabinet-decisions archive 2023/2026 scanned: no AI communiqué online.; Ministries: Searched, nothing found: no AI-specific documents from Health, Education, Justice, Defence, Finance/Tax, Labour or Interior (Health AI lab and civil-servant AI training reported only in media).; Regulators: BNR: regulatory sandbox regulation (AI/ML listed) recorded; 2026 AI risk-management guidelines held as lead (official text not reachable). DPO/NCSA site: compliance tools, no AI guidance. RURA, RISA: no AI-specific documents found (an RURA AI ethics guideline reported by secondary sources was not found on official sites).. Not reached: bnr.rw document listings (script-rendered site; API host returned HTTP 521); ncsa.gov.rw (TLS certificate name mismatch; dpo.gov.rw reached instead). Could not verify: BNR Guidelines No. 52/2026 on AI risk management (official text not reached); Cabinet approval of National AI Agency (8 June 2026) - communiqué not on PMO archive; Cabinet approval date of National AI Policy (20 April 2023). risk-assurance, procurement, cyber-security, transparency, standards, sandbox, sectoral, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found.
